teaser: Six runnable builds, from a doc-research bot to a refund agent with a human gate, each run live against the mock SDK so you see the mechanics.
takeaways: Pick MCP when the systems are shared and owned by other teams; keep an in-process SDK tool when the client is app-private.
Bash is the riskiest tool: run it in a container, block destructive commands with a PreToolUse hook, keep credentials out of the env.
Planner-subagent pattern: the planner holds only the Agent tool; each subagent gets least-privilege tools and its own model.
Per-call policy such as refund thresholds goes in a can_use_tool callback, not a permission mode; enforce it in the backend too and audit.
